title: Held-block NMF separates matched herbal groups, with sparse same-Currier evidence
statement: Starting from Sterneck, Polish and Bowern (2021), compare unsupervised NMF and raw TF-IDF similarity in held-apart, same-section triples. Use only the pinned public practice training pool shared by ZL and Takahashi with matching metadata and at least 50 certain paragraph tokens in each. Within each held-out 16-folio block, match an anchor with a same-hand and a different-hand folio. Require distinct physical folios, both distances at most 12 folios and within two folios of each other, and a maximum token-count ratio of 1.25 across the three pages in both editions. Freeze the common page support before looking at word similarities. Fit each vocabulary, IDF and five-topic NMF in other blocks with one surrounding block on each side excluded. Draw 40 words per page for the primary comparison and 20 for sensitivity, using six fixed seeds.
check: Reproduce the saved scores on the pinned public corpus. For a confirmatory hand-specific test, first identify additional independent same-section and same-Currier blocks with multiple hands, then freeze matching and an independent block-level contrast. Keep the copying and planted-hand controls and compare NMF with raw TF-IDF from the same training-only transform.
source: Rachel Sterneck, Annie Polish and Claire Bowern, Topic Modeling in the Voynich Manuscript (2021), sections 3 and 4.3–4.5. https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02858
findings: The 162-page eligible inventory yields 342 broad matched triples, all herbal, from 39 anchor folios across four held blocks. For 40-word samples the block-averaged same-hand NMF win rates are 86.4% in ZL and 85.8% in Takahashi. Raw TF-IDF gives 84.8% and 81.0%. A pooled copying baseline generated without hand or section labels gives 53.8% and 44.6% for NMF, while adding a fixed 15% planted hand vocabulary gives 93.8% and 93.9%. Requiring the same Currier variety leaves just 10 overlapping comparisons of hands 2 and 5, three anchor folios and two blocks. NMF rates there are 70.0% and 69.4%, driven by one block with 100% wins and one with about 40%. Raw TF-IDF already gives 85.8% and 79.4% on that small subset. The data table includes 20-word, exact-distance and same-side sensitivities.
interpretation: A win means the anchor is closer to the same-hand comparison than to the different-hand comparison in cosine similarity, with half credit for ties. Average triples within each anchor folio, then average folios within block and give each held block equal weight. The broad botanical contrast joins differences in scribal hand and Currier variety. The limited within-B comparisons and unequal block scores leave the magnitude of a hand effect independent of dialect unresolved. Both transcriptions describe the same folios and therefore test transcription sensitivity. Overlapping comparisons are not independent trials. No p-value treating them as independent is reported.
controls: The copying baseline samples a pooled training-only word distribution with one-third probability of copying one of the preceding 30 tokens, resetting the window at each physical block. It preserves the number of tokens per page. The synthetic planted control independently replaces words with hand-specific tokens at probability 15% on the same layout to check that the analysis can carry a handwriting-correlated lexical signal.
reproduction: Write python to nmf_matched.py and results.plan to plan.json. From the pinned checkout run OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONHASHSEED=0 PYTHONPATH=. python3 nmf_matched.py plan.json result.json, with the NumPy and scikit-learn versions in results. The estimator is an unregularized five-topic TF-IDF NMF pilot. Raising the iteration limit from 1,200 to 3,000 eliminated one convergence warning and changed none of the four primary observed 40-word win rates.
